meta.title: Research gaps: cars (audio, interior condition, wheels, labour, pre-purchase inspection) and clothes (resale, repair, shoe life)
meta.method: Every figure carries its source URL, the date read and a method: "page" (fetched and read) or "search-summary" (search-engine result text only, unconfirmed on the page). Null with a reason where nothing was published or nothing could be read. Builds on research-vehicle-shops.json, research-custom-effects.json and research-clothing-services2.json; figures already there are referenced, not repeated.
cautions: AAA's state "repair cost" figures (NY $251.36, CA $271.10, CT $281.53) are not hourly labour rates: they trace to CarMD 2021 check-engine-light repair costs (parts + labour sum to the total). research-vehicle-shops.json labour_rates quotes them with basis unclear; do not use them as $/hour.
KBB and Hagerty grade gaps here are single worked examples, not published fixed gaps.

Practitioner resale-share estimates in research-clothing-services2.json remain blog figures; the Vinted 2025 impact report figure (items sell ~72% below original retail) is the only first-party measured share found.

steren.note: Steren did not surface a CarPlay head unit.

includedCustomPartsAndEquipment.quote: With Progressive, the first $1,000 of damage to aftermarket parts or modifications are covered under auto comprehensive coverage and auto collision coverage.
includedCustomPartsAndEquipment.note: Also on https://www.progressive.com/answers/does-car-insurance-cover-theft/ (page): 'At Progressive, comprehensive coverage will insure up to $1,000 in repair or replacement costs for custom parts and equipment.' Its worked example uses an $800 stereo.

cpeEndorsementTypicalLimit.quote: Custom parts and equipment (CPE) coverage can help pay to repair or replace items that you add to modify your car, like a stereo, navigation system, custom wheels, or even a paint job. CPE coverage typically has a $5,000 limit.

includedLimit.quote: Custom Parts and Equipment: Covers aftermarket parts like custom wheels, stereo systems, or paint jobs if they're damaged in a covered loss.
includedLimit.note: GEICO's page names stereos under the optional CPE coverage but publishes no dollar figure for an included amount. Third-party summaries giving $2,000-$10,000 are industry generalities, not GEICO figures.

audioSublimit.quote: A covered vehicle also includes the parts and equipment that are common to the use of the vehicle as a vehicle.
audioSublimit.note: State Farm Personal Car Policy Booklet, Texas form 9843C (© 2024), text-extracted. No dollar sublimit for audio/sound equipment and no custom-equipment endorsement appears in the physical-damage section; only exclusions found are removable storage media ('tapes, discs, and memory cards'), radar detectors and equipment illegal in the registering jurisdiction. Whether an aftermarket head unit counts as 'common to the use of the vehicle as a vehicle' is not stated. A NY form (9832C) did not download. Null = no published limit, not 'unlimited'.

soundSystemExcludedWithoutEndorsement.quote: We will not cover: ... 8. loss to any sound system in or on an insured auto.
soundSystemExcludedWithoutEndorsement.note: Allstate Auto Policy ACR1 (state not named in the form). Sound System Coverage (Coverage ZA) pays only 'If a premium for Sound System Coverage is shown', at the limit on the Declarations. Crucially, 'Sound System' is defined as a device permanently installed 'in a location other than the one designed by the auto's manufacturer for that type of device' — so a head unit swapped into the factory radio slot is arguably NOT a 'sound system' under this form and would fall to ordinary comp/collision or the custom-parts rule below. A third-party summary of a different Allstate form quoted 'up to $750' for sound systems (search-summary, unverified).

customPartsDefaultLimit.quote: for loss to custom parts or equipment, the higher of $1,000 or the applicable limit shown on the Policy Declarations for Collision Coverage for Custom Equipment or Comprehensive Coverage for Custom Equipment.
customPartsDefaultLimit.note: Custom Parts or Equipment excludes 'items covered under Sound System Coverage'.

Ontario_OAP1_aftermarketElectronicsCap.quote: We will not pay more than $1,500 for loss or damage to electronic accessories or equipment other than factory installed equipment. We will pay the actual cash value of the equipment up to $1,500 in total.
Ontario_OAP1_aftermarketElectronicsCap.note: OAP 1 (2024), s.7.7 What We Will Pay; approved by FSRA for use on or after 2024-01-01. Definition includes 'radios, tape players/decks, stereo players/decks, compact disc players, speakers ... electronic navigation assistance ... and items of a similar nature'. 'Factory installed equipment' = included in the original new purchase price. Note: actual cash value (depreciated), not replacement cost. Standard statutory wording, so it applies to every Ontario insurer (Toronto).

BC_ICBC.note: Already known per brief (ICBC CAD 1,000 cap for permanently attached sound equipment); not re-researched.

Admiral_aftermarketAVEquipmentCap.quote: your vehicle's audio, visual or electronic equipment, as long as it is permanently fitted to your vehicle: Manufacturer equipment is covered in full. Aftermarket equipment is covered up to £1,250 or the market value of your vehicle, whichever is lower.
Admiral_aftermarketAVEquipmentCap.note: Admiral 'Your Car Insurance Guide' AD-003-038 (2024). Same guide, General condition 12: 'Your policy does not cover modifications ... we will only pay the cost of replacing parts needed for your vehicle to meet the manufacturer's specification', and modifications are 'any changes to the way the vehicle looks, functions or drives'; customers must 'tell us beforehand if ... you plan to make any modifications'. So: declare it; Admiral publishes no premium-loading figure for a head-unit swap.

Aviva_accessoriesPermanentlyFitted.quote: accessories. The most we will pay for accessories is shown in your schedule. ... Accessories are items permanently fitted to your car which aren't directly related to how it works as a vehicle. For example, in-built satnavs, cameras, comms kits or roof racks.
Aviva_accessoriesPermanentlyFitted.note: Aviva Online/Aviva Premium wording v7: limit sits on the individual schedule, not in the wording, hence null. Aviva's learner/short-term wording (search-summary, unverified) caps audio/satnav 'up to £500, unless it was fitted by the manufacturer'.

premiumEffectOfHeadUnitSwap.note: No insurer (Admiral, Aviva, Adrian Flux) publishes a premium loading for a stereo/head-unit upgrade. Evidence found is forum anecdote only (mixed: some report no change, some an increase). Aviva and comparethemarket guidance pages returned 403. Declaration requirement already known via the Financial Ombudsman.

AvivaIE_audioCap.quote: We will not pay for: ... 5 any amount over 5% of the insured value of the car, or [€]650, whichever is less, for loss or damage to radio, hi-fi, car-phone or CB radio equipment; 6 any modifications unless they form part of the manufacturers standard specification or are optional extras that we have agreed to cover;
AvivaIE_audioCap.note: Aviva Insurance Ireland DAC MotorCare policy booklet. The cap is the LESSER of 5% of insured value or €650 (e.g. a €8,000 car → €400). The euro sign was lost in PDF extraction. Applies to radio/hi-fi equipment generally, not only aftermarket; modifications are uncovered unless agreed, so a head-unit swap must be declared to be covered at all.

aaaClarification.finding: AAA's 'NY $251.36, CA $271.10' is NOT an hourly labour rate, and on the evidence it is not even labour.

aaaPage.reads: Labels the column 'Average Cost of Labor': NY 251.36, CA 271.10, CT 281.53; says it is 'sourced from World Population Review'; gives no unit or method.

upstream.reads: Source 'Vehicle Health State Index - Car MD', year 2021. Columns read: NY total 135.19 / labor 251.36 / parts 386.55; CA 144.56 / 271.10 / 415.66; CT 136.84 / 281.53 / 418.37.

aaaClarification.interpretation: In every row the first two figures sum exactly to the third (135.19+251.36=386.55; 144.56+271.10=415.66; 136.84+281.53=418.37). So the third is the total. The likeliest reading is that the WPR columns are mislabelled and CarMD's 2021 per-repair figures are labour 135.19 / parts 251.36 / total 386.55 for NY (CA 144.56 / 271.10 / 415.66; CT 136.84 / 281.53 / 418.37). AAA's '$251.36 labour' would then be CarMD's average PARTS cost per check-engine-light repair in 2021. Either way it is per-repair, 2021, check-engine repairs only: not a $/hour figure and not 2026.
